title: Recovery choiceboard and evidence summary — customer-facing
audience: Primary: engineering and product contacts at affected customer accounts. Secondary: customer support and account teams for follow-up.
purpose: Provide a short, clear customer-facing summary of the incident, the recovery choices customers can take, and an evidence package they can use to verify data integrity. This doc is intended for fast publication to status.redwood.ai + email to impacted account reps.
incident_summary: What happened (plain language): Between 2026-06-14 21:22 UTC and 2026-06-15 03:50 UTC, a software deployment introduced a race in the cache population logic during autoscaling. In a subset of steady-state connections, this resulted in duplicated KV cache entries and occasional stale prefix reuse. Symptoms included increased latency, intermittent mis-ordered tokens for streaming responses, and, for ~0.7% of requests during the window, truncated structured responses. The runtime fallback to a secondary model pool was partially effective but did not prevent all user-visible anomalies.
customer_impact: Impacted: customers with long-running streaming sessions or high-concurrency prefix-heavy prompts. Visible effects: slower streaming, occasional token duplication or mis-ordering, and in edge cases truncated JSON/structured outputs. Scope estimate: affecting ~0.7% of requests in EU and US-west regions during the window. No evidence of data exfiltration; authentication and authorization systems remained unaffected.
timeline:
Key timestamps (UTC):
- 2026-06-14 21:22: deployment rollout of runtime v3.4.1 started
- 2026-06-14 21:31: first operator alert: elevated latency from autoscale events
- 2026-06-14 22:05: initial mitigation: paused rollout to remaining hosts
- 2026-06-14 23:10: rollback of v3.4.1 to v3.4.0 completed in primary clusters
- 2026-06-15 00:00: model fallback policy engaged for remaining affected tenants
- 2026-06-15 03:50: final verification completed; traffic normalized
- 2026-06-15 06:00: post-rollback monitoring window closed
(Operators preserved request traces and sampling logs for further forensics.)
operator_actions:
What we did for customers:
- Immediately paused the rollout and rolled back to stable runtime within 45 minutes of first alert.
- Implemented a temporary stricter model-fallback rule to route streaming sessions away from autoscaling hosts showing cache-write races.
- Performed a targeted replay and verification of sampled requests to confirm integrity for the majority of tenant data.
- Captured and archived evidence bundles (sampled request/reply traces + KV cache snapshots) for customer verification where requested.
customer_options:
Choices you can make now (short):
1) Accept our automated reconciliation: we can run a full sampled replay and provide a signed verification bundle. No action required on your side.
2) Request tenant-specific evidence: we will deliver a curated evidence zip (traces + checksums + operator notes) for your security/engineering review.
3) Opt for request-level replay: for customers who want exact reprocessing of a selection of requests (costed option), we can re-run those requests against the stable runtime and provide outputs for diffing.
4) Temporary safety mode: if you wish, we can add your tenant to a temporary safety routing that disables autoscale-induced routing for 72 hours while we complete additional hardening.
replay_instructions:
If you request replay (option 3):
- Send a list of request IDs or example payloads (up to 250 request IDs) to cs-replay@redwood.ai with the subject line 'REPLAY-INC-2026-234 - <TenantName>'.
- We will confirm the replay scope, estimate compute cost, and provide a replay window.
- Replayed outputs will be accompanied by a UUID-signed checksum file.
Notes: replays may produce different outputs for non-deterministic models; we include nonce and seed settings used in the replay to assist verification.
verification_and_integrity:
Evidence we provide:
- Signed trace bundle (GPG-signed): a sampled set of request/response pairs and the operator timeline.
- KV cache snapshot checksums: per-host checksums to show cache divergence and subsequent reconciliation.
- Reconciliation report: short diff analysis highlighting requests with divergent output and classification of divergence type (token-duplication, ordering, truncation).
How to validate: we include instructions and the public key for signature verification; our recommended basic verification steps are in the attached checklist.
apology_and_next_steps:
We are deeply sorry for the disruption. Next steps we are taking:
- Engineering hotfix: root cause fix for cache race scheduled for backport and patch release (v3.4.2) by 2026-06-22.
- Postmortem: full RCA and timeline to be published to our status page and Confluence by 2026-06-27.
- Hardening: expanded autoscale test coverage and new invariant checks for KV write/compare operations.
We will proactively contact named account reps to coordinate any tenant-specific evidence deliveries or replays.
internal_notes:
Draft guidance for account teams (short bullets):
- Prioritize outreach to tenants in our high-concurrency list (attached).
- Offer option 1 by default; escalate to option 2 or 3 on customer request.
- Use subject prefix '[INC-2026-234]' for all related emails.
- Track requests in JIRA-INC-2026-234 as subtask 'customer-evidence-<TenantID>'.
- Engineering owners: Marisol (lead), Liam (replay ops), Evan (forensics).
